- Build: same tree as part B, `git checkout c4196099`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (6 s) + `OS_SKIP_DTS=1 turbo build` of the showcase, CLI and dogfood closures (70 packages, 1 m 10 s, 0 cached) + `env -u OS_SKIP_DTS pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` (spec with `.d.ts`). Node 22.23.4, pnpm 10.31.0, 4 CPUs, 15 GiB shared memory cgroup.
- App: stock showcase via `objectstack dev --seed-admin -p PORT -d file:/tmp/qa3b/RUNNER/db/ITEM.db --no-compile --no-watch` with `OS_PORT=PORT`. Disjoint port ranges 4810–4849, one server per runner at a time. Scratch app copies for the CLI codemod, the connector boots (compiled under their own OS_PORT) and anything that writes into the app. The walled `isolated` / `group` boots for the P0 no-active-org item were started by hand with the posture env vars plus `--no-compile`. `stdio` legs ran on `os start`. The tree's `dist/objectstack.json` and `.objectstack/installed-packages/` were untouched (checked).
- Seed: `--seed-admin` + demo personas. Runtime personas, keys, SCIM connections and service accounts were minted per item through HTTP doors.
- Execution: **parallel**, 4 runner subagents (opus, effort `high`): C1 (2FA, password reset), C2 (keys, SCIM, AI service accounts, P0 no-active-org), C3 (automation, approvals, P0 disable-durable), C4 (MCP incl. P0 stdio, REST, CLI, connectors, import). Pins at `--maxWorkers=1`, dogfood one file per invocation: no OOM kill this time.
- Wall-clock: setup 3 min (10:08–10:11: checkout, install, build, spec dts), done in parallel with drafting the B-api record. Testing 36 min wall (10:11–10:47; per runner C1 14 min, C2 19, C3 22, C4 36, each including 6–7 min of its own reading). Verification 4 min (C1's two security probes re-run on 18.3.0 83d7e4ae). Cost at draft time: `get_session` `external_metadata.usage.cost_usd` = 112.33 for the whole session (B-api + C-api; part B alone was 82.77).

## Extraction (cards drafted, not filed)

## Increment probes (rule 8, on the commits' own doors)

- **c4196099 / #33075, SCIM deactivation revokes API keys (C2, ~6 min).** SCIM `PATCH active:false` revoked all three keys the user owned and stamped each `scim_deactivated`: one live, one self-revoked, one admin-revoked, the earlier reasons restamped. Each key answers `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` with the cannot-be-restored sentence, on REST `GET /data/showcase_task` and on MCP `tools/call`. Another user's key and the admin's key still answer 200. Restore is refused 403 for the owner and for a platform admin, and so is a data-door `PATCH {revoked:false}`. The audit log has one `update` row per key, actor `svc:scim:<connection>`. `PATCH active:true` lifts the ban, the old keys stay revoked, and a newly minted key works. `DELETE /Users/{id}` revokes the new key the same way. The commit's rule holds on every door tried. A revoked key answers 403, not 401, by design (core `api-key.ts`); an unknown key gets 401.
- **9df85e1d / #33076, MCP recall/resubmit (C3).** Over the live MCP endpoint, only the submitter's agent could recall or resubmit, and only after its confirmation step. The approver got FORBIDDEN, a non-participant 404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, and an admin could recall a pending request but not resubmit. The request did not move on any refusal.
- **e003ebbe / #33068, read-only fields named (C3).** A map's answer names the read-only field its items dropped, as one merged entry. A paused subflow child names it too, whether resumed by the parent's run id or its own; in the latter case it shows on the parent's subflow step. The path is reachable only past `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1`, because a stock save refuses any flow writing a read-only field. No clause was scored on that boot.
- **b2322209 / #32931, plugin-form holder package:** console form surface only, so it is not in this api slice (C-browser).
- Per-item probe lines (1–4 min each) are in the group files. They covered boundary values on every identity door (empty, malformed and unknown emails, ids, tokens, codes), half-signed-in and anonymous callers, walled vs single posture, cross-caller import idempotency, and connector fault arms.

## Parked-on #32908 (checklist accuracy and fixture gaps; not extracted)

**Stale or wrong item text, no verdict moved:**
- `identity-auth.two-factor-enrollment-reveal` A4 verify: "a pre-verify bearer answers 401" (#27392) does not hold at c4196099 on either credential (pre-verify get-totp-uri → 200 or 400). The only 401 is the same token used after verify-totp rotated the session. Re-word: "a token minted before the verify answers 401 after it".
- `identity-auth.self-service-password-reset` step 8: the `previous_password_hashes` ring holds only passwords written while `password_history_count > 0`. Also, a PASSWORD_REUSE refusal leaves the token usable.
- `identity-auth.self-service-password-reset` fixture: `/auth/config` reports `features.emailDelivery:false` on stock while reset mail lands in `sys_identity_email` with status `sent`. Don't read it as "no mail".
- `identity-auth.two-factor-disable-lifecycle` step 8 / A5: `mfa_required` has three levels, and a gated user cannot restore the setting (403 MFA_REQUIRED) until they enroll again. The grace stamp is written within the disable and survives re-enrollment.
- `identity-auth.two-factor-backup-codes` fixtures[0]: "one sequence on one boot" isn't needed; each item drove its own enable → verify.
- `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` steps[8]: a plain member's showcase_account create meets the generic CRUD 403, and showcase_task now requires `project`. Name showcase_task (with a project) or showcase_private_note as the tenant-scoped targets. A0 mixes legs of different scorability; scored as A0a–A0c.
- `identity-auth.import-invitation-and-sso-domain-answers` fixtures.requires[2]: the domain doors need `OS_SSO_ENABLED=true` on both boots. `sys_identity_email` has no template-id column.
- `identity-auth.idp-group-permission-set-mapping` steps[3]: with the projected grant present, the hand grant is refused 409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION. Hand-grant first, as the pin's CONTROL does. An unknown set name gets the boundary sentence rather than "no such set".
- `identity-auth.ai-service-account-lifecycle` A0/A2 "both reads answer 200": under the agent ceiling a fresh account's key answers 403 (ADR-0151 D3). Name the grant in fixtures.requires; a built-in ceiling set is refused as a person grant (400).
- **Coverage gap:** no checklist item asserts #33075's SCIM-deactivation key revocation live (unit pins only). C2's probe above is a ready recipe: mint credential → POST /Users → admin set-user-password → keys → PATCH active false/true → DELETE. Its revoked-key answer is 403 `API_KEY_REVOKED`, not 401.
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` (9df85e1d): "anyone else is refused (FORBIDDEN)" — a caller who cannot read the request gets 404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND first. That is the safer behaviour; only the wording is imprecise.
- #33068 reachability: `droppedFields` over HTTP needs a fixture past the lint (`OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` or a pre-rule stored flow). A future item should name it.
- `automation.trigger-status-contract` A5: only the deregistration arm was driven, as in part B.
- `automation.flow-run-semantics-v18` steps[1]: `qa_elevated` has no recipe body (autolaunched, runAs system, create_record was used).
- `api-backend.route-ledger-live-parity`: 16 route ledgers, not 11. REST_ROUTE_LEDGER has 20 families. `POST /data/:object/actions/:name` is correctly a routing 404; don't sample it as a ledger row.
- `api-backend.api-methods-verb-gate` A1 prose: restore/purge follow from `delete` (unchanged since part B).
- `cli.migrate-meta-codemod` step 7: two mode-less decisions, not three. `--from 17 --to 19` says nothing about 18 → 19 having no step.
- `ai.mcp-run-action-exposure-gate`: admin `list_actions` is 47 entries (Mei 35), against 45/33 at 8e3d4a54. The clause allows it.
- `records-forms.named-import-mapping` A1: say "idempotent per caller". A member re-importing the admin's file creates duplicates on the private-OWD object because the upsert match sees only the caller's rows. That is RLS working.
- `ai.mcp-oauth-private-host-transport` steps[3] (real client from a second machine) stays blocked(fixture); it scores no clause.

**Environment facts for RUNNER:**
- `scripts/qa/qa-fixture.mjs walled-boot` runs `os dev` without `--no-compile`, so on a shared checkout it rewrites `examples/app-showcase/dist/objectstack.json` under every other runner. Pass `--no-compile` there, and have RUNNER's walled-boot entry say so.
- `cd APP && setsid cmd &` records the subshell's pid, so `kill -- -PID` misses the server. Record `$!` of a bare `setsid … &` (C4's slip, fixed mid-run; no verdict rests on it).
- Run vitest at `--maxWorkers=1` with dogfood one file per invocation. With 4 runners this gave no OOM kills, against repeated kills with 8 runners at `--maxWorkers=2` in part B.
